factsAccepted: Earnings are solid but the realizable multiple hinges on diligence-readiness and earnings quality. EBITDA is ~$11M at a 13% margin with modest net debt (~$8M) and a 7-month backlog. Comps suggest ~5-7x EBITDA from financial buyers and ~7-10x from strategics for assets with durable aftermarket and clean diligence. But there is no recent quality-of-earnings study and statements are unaudited, so normalized EBITDA and the achievable multiple are not yet substantiated, leaving a wide and unverified valuation range.

The dominant transferability risk is key-person and succession dependence. There is no internal CEO successor, and senior engineering plus the top-5 customer relationships (~38% of revenue) are concentrated in the founder and 2-3 long-tenured leaders. A buyer's price and a retain-and-hire plan both depend on how much value survives the founder's exit, which is currently undocumented. This is the central driver of both the achievable multiple and the feasibility of an owner exit within 24 months.

The higher-margin aftermarket stream (~30% of revenue, ~28% gross vs ~21% on machinery) is the most valuable and most scrutinized asset, but its durability is uncharacterized. It is unknown whether this stream is contracted/recurring or relationship-dependent and therefore at risk in a transition. Buyers (especially strategics paying a premium) will price the aftermarket heavily on its proven recurrence and stickiness through an ownership change.

Path feasibility differs sharply by buyer type and by the founder's constraints. A financial buyer offers a faster, standardized process but typically expects management continuity or an earn-out the founder cannot personally provide past 24 months, and prices on multiple. A strategic buyer could pay a synergy premium but may integrate or relocate the plant (conflicting with the workforce/reputation constraint) and is harder to source. Retaining requires hiring a credible professional manager into a key-person-dependent business and defers liquidity. None of the three can be ranked without substantiated transferable value and aftermarket durability.

The owner's actual after-tax outcome under each path is unquantified. Multiple, structure (cash vs earn-out vs rollover equity), tax treatment, and the founder's personal liquidity needs combine differently across A, B, and C, so the option that maximizes after-tax, risk-adjusted proceeds within the founder's constraints cannot be identified from headline multiples alone.
factsNeedingClarification: Substantiated quality-of-earnings: normalized EBITDA after owner add-backs, one-time items, and working-capital adjustments to buyer standard
Transferable vs key-person-dependent value: how much revenue/margin survives the founder's and senior leaders' departure, and how durable the top-5 relationships are without them
Aftermarket durability: whether the ~30% aftermarket stream is contracted/recurring or relationship-dependent and at risk in a transition
Strategic-buyer landscape: which strategics would pay a synergy premium, and whether they would preserve or relocate the plant/workforce
Owner's after-tax net proceeds and personal liquidity needs under each structure (multiple, earn-out, rollover equity, tax treatment)
